prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies transformer/feeder bays under approved designs/limits. Elements: Bay Automation Controller (Juniper), North Bay Controller, South Bay Controller automate bays; Juniper applies permissives/interlocks, produces Bay Status Digest. Breaker Control Unit executes authorized, interlocked operations. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) independently protects feeder, produces Relay Diagnostic Note. Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing) presents/consolidates indications/communications quality, produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; never substitutes local indications/protection. Station Gateway carries authorized external supervisory communications. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) distributes time, produces Clock Drift Snapshot at configured offset. Sequence Event Archive (Orchard), authoritative event-evidence repository, preserves received records: source, event/receipt times, available quality. Engineering Workstation restricts access to assigned engineers, revision-controls configurations/history, produces Settings Review Receipt. Maintenance Remote Terminal provides approved maintenance access, not local authority. Station DC System powers automation/protection; loss interrupts visibility/timing. Actors: Control Room Operator verifies commands, coordinates access, may suspend work, evaluates field conditions before automation resumes. Switching Desk Coordinator confirms switching/clearances and handback. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) develops/documents changes. Substation Supervisor authorizes changes, confirms work/operating-condition/procedure compatibility, escalates availability. Substation Field Crew (Cinder) inspects/maintains/switches under authorization; sends Breaker Inspection Tag recording condition/time. Requirements: Local selection/interlocks prevail; remote commands require authority/selection/permissions/availability; control failure cannot inhibit trips. Communications loss makes displays stale/unavailable; verify recovery currency. Timing supports correlation, not protection; device-specific holdover/clocks and synchronized/degraded/unavailable quality apply. Settings: study/equipment basis, documented effects, unique prereview revision, upstream/downstream coordination, independent qualified completeness/consistency/suitability/calculation/logic/applicability review; copying insufficient. Record approval; verify model/firmware; approved outage/window; compare installed/approved settings, functionally test; resolve/review discrepancies before release. Work: authorization/site-entry checks; review scope/route/hazards/communications; log arrival/departure; establish boundaries; verify identity against documents and position/isolation/hazardous-energy absence—not screens/automation alone. Discrepancies unsafe until resolved; promptly report uncertainty. Maintain communications; loss stops affected work under hold/escalation procedure. Completion requires accounting
